thread:
zoe: Heads-up — ran into a weird combo while setting up the sample app. I imported an old `profiles.json` from my laptop and now `redwoodctl` complains about duplicate profile ids and refuses to pick an active profile. Also `redwoodctl serve --local` crashes because port 8080 is in use.

paul: Duplicate ids usually happen if someone copies profiles.json without updating the `id` field. Which version of ctl are you on? `redwoodctl version` and can you paste the first ~20 chars of `profiles.json`?

zoe: Version 0.13.1. profiles.json starts with: {"profiles":[{"id":"a1b2c3","name":"work"}... then another entry with same id. I edited name locally but left id. I tried `redwoodctl profile set-active work` and it still says "conflict: multiple profiles match".

mina: We should add a merge helper. For now you can run `jq` to rewrite unique ids: `jq '.profiles |= map(.id = (uuidgen))' ~/.config/redwoodctl/profiles.json` then `redwoodctl list-profiles` should show distinct ids. But backup first.

zoe: I don't have uuidgen on WSL; used `python -c 'import uuid,sys;print(uuid.uuid4())'` and patched. That fixed the duplicate id error. Thanks.

paul: About port 8080 — `redwoodctl serve --local` defaults to 8080. If another process uses it you'll see a crash. Try `redwoodctl serve --local --port 0` to pick a free port or `--port 3000`. Also we'll add a friendlier error if bind fails.

zoe: Good tip. I set `--port 0` and got a weird auth hiccup: the device-code flow opened the browser but the CLI returned `auth: retry limit reached` after a couple retries. The network here is flaky (hotel wifi) but the browser flow succeeded. The CLI didn't pick up the token.

mina: Retry limit reached could be exponential backoff combined with a hard max. Which version again? We changed the retry behavior in 0.13.0 to be more tolerant, but older ones bail.

zoe: 0.13.1 — maybe still bails. The CLI logs show intermittent 502s from the auth proxy and then `poll: token not found`.

paul: We should improve observability: log poll attempt numbers and server error codes. For immediate workaround, use `redwoodctl login --poll-interval 5s --timeout 180s` (these flags exist in 0.13.2+). If you can't upgrade, use the web callback mode: `redwoodctl login --web-callback` which waits for a direct POST from the auth server to localhost.

zoe: I couldn't bind the callback port because of docker forwarding, but `--poll-interval` isn't present in 0.13.1. I ended up upgrading the binary to 0.13.3 and reran `redwoodctl login --timeout 180s` and it worked.

ops-bot: Created internal issue #2897: "ctl: add profile-merge helper + better duplicate-id error" assigned to @paul.

paul: I'll add a small `redwoodctl profile dedupe` subcommand that detects dup ids and offers to reassign new uuids or merge metadata. Also will make the serve error print which PID is using the port with a hint for `lsof -i :8080`.

mina: For the auth retry corner case, let's make the polling more resilient: respect HTTP 5xx as retryable and extend timeouts when network errors appear. Also add a `REDWOODCTL_POLL_MODE=callback|poll` env var to prefer web callback when localhost bind works.

zoe: Lovely. Final note: the quickstart script should check `profiles.json` sanity before starting and auto-select last-used profile if only one exists. I almost filed a support ticket.

devex-bot: Opened docs ticket #2930: "quickstart: sanity-check profiles.json and auto-select last-used profile" assigned to @mina :spiral_note_pad:

zoe: Thanks for the quick help, everyone. Upgrading the binary and patching profiles made onboarding smooth again.

paul: Thanks for the repro and the logs — very actionable. We'll follow up on the CLI UX fixes. :thumbsup:
